mcqs.stem: A synthetic adult patient presents with acute urinary retention and suprapubic discomfort. The teaching case contains no real patient information.
mcqs.lead_in: Which immediate management principle should be prioritized?

options.label: A
options.text: Assess and relieve retention using an appropriate clinical pathway
options.rationale: The option addresses the immediate problem in the synthetic scenario.

options.label: B
options.text: Defer all assessment until outpatient review
options.rationale: This does not address the acute presentation.

options.label: C
options.rationale: The option is not directed at the immediate problem.

options.label: D
options.rationale: The option is unsafe and unsupported.

mcqs.answer_rationale: Synthetic educational rationale only; faculty must verify the clinical content against current local guidance.
mcqs.distractor_rationale: Each distractor has an explicit reason for being less appropriate.

osce_stations.candidate_instructions: Take a focused history from a simulated patient with urinary symptoms.
osce_stations.role_player_brief: Use only the supplied synthetic script; do not improvise identifying details.
osce_stations.examiner_instructions: Observe communication, focused history and safety-netting.

checklist.criterion: Introduces self and confirms simulated patient identity

critical_actions: Recognizes red-flag features and escalates appropriately
osce_stations.global_rating_scale: 1–5 anchored scale; anchors to be faculty-authored.
osce_stations.marking_rubric: Local faculty rubric; review before use.

challenges.case_stem: Synthetic progressive case: an adult presents with a new urinary symptom.
challenges.explanation: Explain the reasoning and uncertainty; cite a current verified source before approval.
challenges.differential_rationale: Explain why plausible alternatives are less likely without implying certainty.
challenges.provenance: Original synthetic faculty-authored case; no third-party content.
